clue.text: Calm head needed to absorb endless material

indicators.note: to absorb is to take something inside, so one piece is swallowed by the other

parts.note: pate is an old word for the top of the head

indicators.note: something endless has lost its final part, so the word for material is cut short

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: A composed leader is wanted to soak up some unfinished fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a leader but is the top of the skull; the cut-short fabric sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to soothe or pacify them, a synonym of the verb calm.

clue.text: Soldier expected to remove uniform for march

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: removing takes something away, so a letter is dropped from the word for expected

parts.note: a train that is expected is due
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to take off his uniform before a march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing but is the phonetic-alphabet letter, removed from the word for expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a ceremonial procession of troops, so it is a noun for a march.

clue.text: Claim member is guzzling beer? On the contrary

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing, so one word takes the other inside it
on the contrary flips who swallows whom, so the drink holds the limb rather than the reverse

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a leg is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: An accusation that a club member has been knocking back beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the member swallows the beer; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles, so the beer goes around the member.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, which is to claim it.

clue.text: One selling lots of our nice tea abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered far and wide, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sells large quantities of our good tea overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like a quantity of tea but means items at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer conducts sales where goods are offered in numbered lots to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Spielberg film which laid bare moral belief

indicators.note: laying something bare strips its covering, so the outside letters of the word are removed

parts.note: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial was directed by Steven Spielberg
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spielberg movie that exposed someone's moral convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' looks like a relative pronoun but is the word to strip of its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a principle of right conduct, a moral belief someone holds.

clue.text: Award given to American journalist caused puzzlement

parts.note: BEM is the British Empire Medal
US is the standard abbreviation for American
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A US reporter receiving a prize left people baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Empire Medal is a British honour, abbreviated BEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means bewildered; the clue treats it as a past-tense verb, having puzzled someone.

clue.text: Note reptile briefly accessing container upsetting seed

parts.note: B is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the column upside down, so the joined pieces read from bottom to top
briefly means cut short, so the creature's name loses its final letter

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
a lizard is a reptile

explanation.surface: A short reptile clambering into an upturned box with a seed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upsetting' turns the cask-plus-reptile chunk upside down; the note stays on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil nut is the large edible seed of a South American tree.

clue.text: Hard to follow this writer's essentially frightening story

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed at the end

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: belonging to me

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of a word, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the eleven
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A writer admits his scary story is hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional tale, often of gods or heroes, so it is a kind of story.

clue.text: Young bird's narrow escape close to Yorkshire river

parts.note: a narrow squeak is a narrow escape

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A fledgling has a lucky escape near a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'near' but takes the last letter of Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeaker is a dictionary term for a young bird, especially a young pigeon, named for its cry.

clue.text: Foolish types detailed dim attempt to head north

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: dingy means dim and gloomy

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means travelling upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to have a stab is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: Silly people gave detailed instructions for a feeble attempt to go north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'thorough' but is read as de-tailed: DINGY loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingbats is informal slang for stupid or eccentric people, i.e. foolish types.

clue.text: Souvenir from French island King carries back

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the combined letters are read right to left
to carry something is to hold it, so the monarch's letters go around the island

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles
ile is French for island

explanation.surface: A king brings home a memento from an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: CR, Carolus Rex, is King Charles's royal cipher; the whole container is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept from the past as a reminder, much like a keepsake or souvenir.

clue.text: Ben and Arthur treated for bad indigestion

indicators.note: something treated has been processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two men, Ben and Arthur, got medical treatment for a nasty stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartburn is a burning pain in the chest caused by stomach acid, a common symptom of indigestion.

clue.text: Dietary supplement for a boxer?

parts.note: surface reading: a vitamin or protein shake for a prize-fighter
setter's reading: a boxer is also a breed of dog, so its treat is a crunchy snack from a pet shop

explanation.walkthrough: A boxer is a breed of dog as well as a fighter; the question mark flags the switch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard baked snack given to pet dogs is a dietary extra for a boxer, the canine breed.

clue.text: Post stuff that's read out

indicators.note: reading something out means saying it, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to jam is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Instructions to pack items into the post and read the label aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail, but it is the upright of a door frame; the B is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical side post of a door or window frame.

clue.text: Occasionally admits hospital worker is drunk's partner?

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective paired with drunk in a phrase

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
an orderly is a hospital attendant

explanation.surface: A hospital worker sometimes lets in a patient who is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk and disorderly' is the British police charge, so this word is drunk's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal charge 'drunk and disorderly' pairs the two words, so the answer is the companion of drunk.

clue.text: When tipsy, nine starting to become pig-headed

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: After a few drinks, nine people start turning stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' looks like a first-letter signal but is part of the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent means refusing to compromise, which matches being obstinate or stubborn.

clue.text: Adaptation of Uris novel brings disgust

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks an original into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film version of a Leon Uris book provokes a strong reaction of disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: Leon Uris wrote Exodus; his name is only letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Revulsion is a strong feeling of loathing, a close synonym for disgust.

clue.text: Goalposts just stopping United getting points, gutted!

parts.note: U is short for United in team names

indicators.note: stopping a gap means filling it, so this word plugs the space inside the other
a gutted fish has had its insides removed, so only the outer letters survive

parts.note: first and last letters
right and just both mean fair

explanation.surface: United are gutted to fail to win, with the ball hitting the woodwork.
explanation.walkthrough: RIGHT sits between the P and S, after U.
explanation.definitionFit: The uprights are the two vertical posts of a goal in rugby or football, so the word names goalposts.

clue.text: Face of Sue after receiving makeover

indicators.note: a makeover remodels someone's appearance, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: How Sue's face looked once the beauticians had worked on her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a time word but is part of the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Your features are the parts of your face — eyes, nose, mouth — so the plural word stands for the face itself.

clue.text: Repair piano with expression of doubt

parts.note: P is the musical marking for piano, softly
to have reservations is to have doubts
joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: Fixing a piano while voicing some misgivings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, as in a house in good repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair as a noun means condition or upkeep, and preservation is the keeping of something in good order.

clue.text: One after another graduate trainee on the telephone

indicators.note: on the phone we only hear words, so this is about how a word sounds

parts.note: an intern is a recent graduate on a training placement

explanation.surface: A graduate trainee working the phones, taking calls one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in turn means taking them in sequence, each following the previous.

clue.text: Place for captain in game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the raised platform from which a ship is commanded
second meaning: the card game for four players in pairs

explanation.surface: A team captain's spot in the line-up of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captain' suggests a sports team but means a ship's captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain stands on the bridge, and bridge is also a trick-taking card game.

clue.text: Greek character hid outlaw from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means at intervals, so only every second letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A Greek figure sometimes sheltered a bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person but means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Hancock's role formerly, one augmenting vital NHS supplies?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Tony Hancock's character in a famous 1961 television comedy episode of that name
second meaning: a person who gives life-saving fluid to hospitals

explanation.walkthrough: Hancock is the comedian Tony Hancock, not the politician; 'The Blood Donor' is his best-known sketch. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedy episode was titled after his role, and a person giving blood tops up the health service's vital stocks.

clue.text: Group of eight from company raised small amount

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the letters upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: A firm has raised a modest sum from eight investors.
explanation.definitionFit: An octad is a set of eight things, from the Greek prefix for eight.

clue.text: What planes do with load heading for Ibiza

parts.note: to tax is to burden, or load

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Aircraft carrying cargo bound for the Spanish holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like a flight's destination but takes Ibiza's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft taxi when they move slowly along the ground to or from the runway.

clue.text: Gather Bali's tourists will include medicinal plant collector

indicators.note: the earlier words include the answer within them, held across their letters

parts.note: runs across the three words

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers in Bali will pick up a healer who gathers herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Bali's is ignored when reading the letters through.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist gathers and uses plants for remedies, so is a collector of medicinal plants.

clue.text: Circular series of holes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shaped like a circle
second meaning: a complete game of golf, played over eighteen holes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like a leaflet, and the holes sound like perforations, but the second meaning is golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A round shape is circular, and a round of golf is played over a set course of holes.

clue.text: Succeeded blocking reports about meeting

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word is read backwards
blocking means standing in the way, so a letter is lodged inside the word

parts.note: reports are loud bangs, or noises
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A successor stalled reports on a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reports' looks like documents but means bangs; reversed, it takes S in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a period when a group meets to do business, i.e. a meeting.

clue.text: Senior female doctor annoyed, denied advanced drug

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
being denied means being refused, so this letter is withheld from the word

parts.note: taken as written
A is short for advanced, as in A-level
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An irritated senior woman doctor refused an experimental drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like part of 'female doctor' but is the anagram signal; ANNOYED without A, plus E, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or longest-serving woman in a field, so a senior female.
